countingPolicy.normalisation: NFC and case folding; preserve macrons
countingPolicy.senses: One spelling can require several assessed readings without automatically adding to the vocabulary total.
countingPolicy.forms: Variant spellings, singular/plural relations and passive forms require explicit review before distinct counts.
countingPolicy.phrases: Keep multiword constructions, job titles and kiwaha separate from distinct single-word vocabulary.
countingPolicy.repeat: Previously introduced items recur without being counted again.

groups.title: Identity and people
groups.rationale: Introduce and identify people; teach pronoun distinctions in context.

groups.title: Belonging and places
groups.rationale: Origin and present location. Do not equate the lake and inside readings of roto.

groups.title: Naming and describing
groups.rationale: Use concrete referents and simple descriptions.

groups.title: Numbers and quantities
groups.rationale: Count things and people using the appropriate constructions.

groups.title: Introducing your work
groups.rationale: Start with useful single word occupations. Agency job title phrases remain separate expressions.

groups.title: Everyday actions
groups.structureFocus: i / kua / kei te / e … ana / ka / me
groups.rationale: Introduce the action reading of each word in supported sentences, reusing Level 1 vocabulary.

groups.title: Food and daily routines
groups.rationale: Practical conversation choices. Unranked items require a usefulness reason, not an invented rank.

groups.title: Time and position
groups.rationale: Teach the intended time or position meaning explicitly; single spellings can serve different functions.

groups.title: Needs and responses
groups.rationale: Ask for help and explain needs, without treating negative markers as freely interchangeable.

groups.title: Instructions
groups.rationale: Select and verify command and passive forms per verb before creating exercises.

groups.title: Objects used in tasks
groups.rationale: Give meaningful instructions with known actions and practical objects.

groups.title: Possession and responsibility
groups.rationale: Readings and a/o relationships require their own teaching targets. Known spellings do not count as new words again.

groups.title: Work and shared responsibilities
groups.rationale: Explain who is responsible and who things are for. Verify each chosen structure fit.

groups.title: Belongings and resources
groups.rationale: Reuse known nouns in possession contexts; do not count them again.

groups.title: Comparison and qualities
groups.rationale: Compare qualities. Resolve spelling variants and the easy/light versus mother readings.

groups.title: Ability and habits
groups.structureFocus: ka taea e / kāore e taea e / verb + ai
groups.rationale: Use ability and habit structures with already familiar actions; unsupported words stay pending.

groups.title: Actions from another perspective
groups.rationale: These are form targets. Do not automatically inflate the distinct vocabulary total with every passive spelling.

groups.title: Questions and explanations
groups.rationale: Multiword question frames belong with structures, not the single word count.

groups.title: Conditions and discussion
groups.rationale: Teach condition and explanation frames as linked constructions, not interchangeable tokens.

groups.title: Stories, community and opinions
groups.rationale: Integrate earlier vocabulary in useful discussion; identify new senses separately from new words.

vocabulary.frequencySenseNote: The frequency PDF glosses the barking reading; this course group intends the frequency or repetition reading. Do not treat the source band as sense-specific evidence.

kiwaha.teachingMeaning: A positive reaction to something impressive.
kiwaha.usageNote: Teach as a conversational response, not a word by word translation.
Can also convey fear or a negative reaction. Include context and delivery.
Can sound dismissive. Do not use a trivial reassurance scenario to teach dismissing serious concerns.
Can also criticise. Initial practice must make the intended supportive use clear.
Treat the whole expression as the target, not a literal location statement.

kiwaha.teachingMeaning: Signal that your statement may need correcting.
kiwaha.usageNote: This idiomatic reading must remain distinct from the beneficiary reading of māna.
